# Choose a method from the study, not a menu

## Decision sequence

1. Define the estimand.
2. Identify the independent sampling or assignment unit.
3. Classify the outcome.
4. Map pairing, repeated measures, nesting, blocking, and time.
5. Decide whether the goal is explanation, causal inference, or prediction.
6. Choose a model family.
7. Predefine contrasts and diagnostics.

## Starting map

| Outcome / question | Independent observations | Dependent or clustered observations |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous, 2 groups | Welch t test / linear model | paired t test / linear mixed model |
| Continuous, >2 groups | ANOVA / linear model | repeated-measures or mixed model |
| Binary | logistic regression | mixed logistic model / GEE |
| Counts with exposure | Poisson; check dispersion | mixed Poisson or negative binomial |
| Overdispersed counts | negative-binomial regression | negative-binomial mixed model |
| Proportion from successes/trials | binomial model | beta-binomial or mixed binomial |
| Alpha diversity | regression appropriate to metric | mixed model where repeated |
| Community composition | ordination for exploration; PERMANOVA for a test | restricted permutations / longitudinal methods |
| Taxon-wise abundance | count/compositional model + FDR | design-aware model + FDR |
| Prediction | held-out evaluation | group-aware or time-aware validation |

This table is an entry point, not an automatic selector. Detection limits,
structural zeros, nonlinear effects, unequal variance, small cluster counts, and
batch effects can change the recommendation.

## Common mismatches

### PCA versus PERMANOVA

PCA is an ordination: it represents directions of variance under Euclidean
geometry. It does not provide a treatment p-value. PERMANOVA tests whether
group centroids differ in a chosen distance space, but dispersion differences
can affect interpretation and must be checked.

### Paired versus independent t test

Before/after samples from the same system are paired. Pairing models within-unit
differences and usually reduces irrelevant baseline variation. An independent
t test discards that structure and uses the wrong standard error.

### ANOVA versus many t tests

ANOVA provides an omnibus test of a predefined factor while controlling the
single family-level test. Planned contrasts answer specific scientific
questions. Unadjusted pairwise t tests inflate false-positive risk.

### Ordinary regression versus mixed model

Ordinary regression assumes residual independence after conditioning on
predictors. Repeated measurements within a tank usually violate this. A mixed
model can represent the shared tank-level variation and estimate population and
tank-level effects together.

## Minimum reporting set

For every result, report:

- biological estimand and experimental unit;
- model formula, outcome distribution, and link;
- effect estimate in interpretable units;
- confidence/credible interval;
- testing procedure and multiplicity correction;
- assumption and diagnostic checks;
- software and version;
- sensitivity analyses that changed the conclusion.
